title: Morgan Wallen Returns to No. 1, Charli xcx Earns Top Three Debut on Albums Chart
description: Morgan Wallen has returned to No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with “I’m the Problem” for a 14th non-consecutive week, while Charli xcx debuts at No. 3 wi
body:
Morgan Wallen has returned to No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with “I’m the Problem” for a 14th non-consecutive week, while Charli xcx debuts at No. 3 with her eighth album “Music, Fashion, Film.”

	“I’m the Problem,” which was released more than a year ago, ticks from No. 3 to 1 on this week’s chart with 80,000 equivalent album units. The album initially debuted at No. 1 in May 2025. Wallen, who is currently on his “Still the Problem” stadium tour, recently dropped his new single “Been By Now,” which is a standalone track and not included in the album’s latest tally.
	

	Charli xcx, meanwhile, earns her fourth top 10 as “Music, Fashion, Film” bows at No. 3 with 78,000 equivalent album units, marking her biggest debut by that metric. Earlier this year, her soundtrack for “Wuthering Heights” debuted at No. 8, and with her latest, the pop star becomes the only woman and third act overall to have at least two debuts in the top 10 this year. Previously, Drake earned three concurrent debuts with “Iceman,” “Habibti” and “Maid of Honour,” while Ateez had two debuts with “Golden Hour : Part.4” and “Golden Hour : Part.5.”


	Elsewhere in the top five, Olivia Rodrigo’s “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love” holds steady at No. 2, while Ella Langley’s “Dandelion” and Noah Kahan’s “The Great Divide” maintain at Nos. 4 and 5.

	Rounding out the top 10 are Drake’s “Iceman,” Wallen’s “One Thing at a Time,” Michael Jackson’s “Thriller,” Olivia Dean’s “The Art of Loving” and Kahan’s “Stick Season.”

title: ‘Hadestown’ Parts Ways With Hades Actor Geno Segers After Online Controversy
description:
Geno Segers, who was announced this week to join Broadway’s “Hadestown,” will no longer be part of the Broadway production.

	“Hadestown” announced
body:
Geno Segers, who was announced this week to join Broadway’s “Hadestown,” will no longer be part of the Broadway production.

	“Hadestown” announced a new principal cast earlier this week, with Segers set to play Hades. His previous stage credits include “On the Town” and “The Lion King” as well as TV roles in “Banshee,” “Pair of Kings” and “Yellowstone.”

	The news that Segers is no longer joining the cast comes after online comments and videos resurfaced on theater blogs this week. Segers previously posted videos that some viewed as anti-transgender and critical of pronoun usage. The actor also allegedly criticized trans athletes participating in women’s sports.
	

	The “Hadestown” producers said in a statement Sunday: “The producers of ‘Hadestown’ and Geno Segers have mutually agreed that Mr. Segers will no longer join the Broadway production. Additional casting will be announced shortly.”


	Segers has made his Instagram account private and removed videos from his YouTube channel.

	The new principal cast of “Hadestown” will begin their run Sept. 1 at Broadway’s Walter Kerr Theatre. The cast features pop-rock musician Kayko as Orpheus, Jasmin Savoy Brown (“Yellowjackets,” “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma”) as Eurydice, Norbert Leo Butz (“Catch Me If You Can,” “Dirty Rotten Scoundrels,” “Wicked”) as Hermes and Amber Iman (“Lempicka,” “Goddess”) as Persephone.

	“Hadestown” was written by Anaïs Mitchell. Through folk and jazz music, the show combines the Greek myth of Orpheus and Eurydice with the myth of Hades and Persephone. 
	

	The show began its Broadway run in 2019 and opened on London’s West End in 2024. A live stage capture of the production, filmed with the original principal cast in London in early 2025, premiered in theaters for a limited release on July 24.

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Obliterates Expectations With $927 Million Global Debut
description:
All hail Peter Parker.

	Sony and Marvel’s web-slinging adventure “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” climbed to $927 million globally, a mind-blowing, jaw-
body:
All hail Peter Parker.

	Sony and Marvel’s web-slinging adventure “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” climbed to $927 million globally, a mind-blowing, jaw-dropping and totally epic opening weekend haul. Few films manage to earn that much by the end of their box office runs, much less after three days on the big screen. It’s the second-largest worldwide debut of all time, trailing only 2019’s Marvel titan “Avengers: Endgame” with $1.2 billion. Those titles reign far above the third-biggest global opening, which belongs to 2018’s “Avengers: Infinity War” with $640 million globally.
	

	“Brand New Day,” the fourth comic-book adaptation starring Tom Holland as Marvel’s friendly, neighborhood Spider-Man, opened to $572 million internationally from 66 markets, as well as $355 million at the domestic box office. Overseas, China secured the biggest start with $121 million, followed by the United Kingdom with $49 million, Mexico with $38.3 million and South Korea with $25 million. The movie set opening-weekend benchmarks in several individual territories, including France with $26.6 million, India with $31.8 million, Brazil with $23.8 million and Spain with $15.6 million.


	With such a significant launch in China, “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” is poised to eventually surpass $2 billion at the global box office — a milestone that only seven movies in history have ever surpassed. “Spider-Man: No Way Home,” the predecessor to “Brand New Day,” managed to generate a staggering $1.9 billion in 2021 without playing in China. Although the country has been hit-or-miss with recent Hollywood blockbusters, Peter Parker still resonates with mainland audiences. 
	

	Premium large formats have been all the rage, and audiences were eager to watch “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” on some of the biggest and brightest screens. Although the movie didn’t play on Imax, where Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” has the entire network for three weekends, “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” established new records for Dolby ($10 million domestically), 4DX ($17 million globally) and ScreenX ($14.4 million globally).

	Destin Daniel Cretton (“Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings”) directed “Brand New Day,” which takes place after Peter Parker made the difficult decision to erase himself from everyone’s memory at the end of “No Way Home.” All the action picks up as a mysterious entity threatens New York City. Meanwhile, Spider-Man is struggling with his mutating powers — and the fact that his girlfriend MJ (Zendaya) and best friend Ned (Jacob Batalon) are making memories at MIT with zero recollection of their former pal. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has great reviews and positive audience scores, earning a 90% on Rotten Tomatoes and “A” grade on CinemaScore exit polls. Without much competition, the comic-book sequel is poised to dominate on the big screen throughout the rest of summer.

	“We’re incredibly grateful to audiences for embracing the bold, creative and deeply emotional vision Destin took with this film,” says producer Amy Pascal. “It’s exciting to see such a powerful response to a story that never lost sight of what makes Peter Parker so enduring—his humanity. This remarkable opening reinforces that moviegoers are hungry for stories that are both spectacular and deeply human, and we’re thrilled to see that resonate on such a global scale.”

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Swings to Mind-Blowing $355 Million Debut, Second-Biggest Opening Weekend in Box Office History
description:
With great power comes truly heroic ticket sales.

	Sony and Marvel‘s comic book adventure “Brand New Day” obliterated box office expectations, coll
body:
With great power comes truly heroic ticket sales.

	Sony and Marvel‘s comic book adventure “Brand New Day” obliterated box office expectations, collecting a jaw-dropping $355 million from 4,487 North American theaters. It’s the second-biggest debut in domestic box office history, following 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame” with $357 million, not adjusted for inflation. “Brand New Day” could end up eclipsing the all-time record if Monday’s final tally lands above estimates. No other films have ever come close to surpassing $300 million in a single weekend. The third-largest domestic opening belongs to 2021’s “Spider-Man: No Way Home” with $260 million, followed by 2018’s “Avengers: Infinity War” with $257 million. Yes, Marvel Studios now boasts the four largest openings of all time at the domestic box office. 
	

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” collected $573 million at the international box office, bringing the grand total to a staggering $927 million worldwide and underscoring Peter Parker’s broad, global appeal. It’ll rank as the second-biggest worldwide debut after “Endgame,” which captured a mind-blowing $1.2 billion in its first weekend of release. Sony spent around $225 million to produce “Brand New Day,” not including marketing costs. Destin Daniel Cretton (“Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings”) directed “Brand New Day,” which has garnered euphoric reactions from critics and audiences. It holds a 90% on Rotten Tomatoes and “A” grade on CinemaScore exit polls.


	“This is a truly phenomenal opening, and we are grateful to audiences everywhere for coming out and experiencing our film the way it was meant to be seen,” said Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige, who produced the movie. “This debut reflects the enduring power of Marvel’s characters, and the connection they continue to have with fans around the world — and, as audiences saw, it sets up exciting things to come.”
	

	Even with the craze surrounding “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” remained a draw with $51 million in its third frame. Together, they have fueled the biggest collective weekend in box office history with roughly $430 million across all films. The top weekend prior to this was, of course, “Avengers: Endgame” ($402 million collectively), followed by “Avengers: Infinity War” ($314 million collectively).

	Few in Hollywood had expected another movie to near the initial box office heights of “Avengers: Endgame,” which was touted as the epic culmination of 22 interconnected films. After the history-making finale of “Endgame,” Marvel experienced its first-ever bout of superhero fatigue with sequels such as 2023’s “The Marvels” and “Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania” and 2025’s “Captain America: Brave New World,” “Thunderbolts*” and “The Fantastic Four: First Steps” all disappointing at the box office. There were hits, like “No Way Home,” 2022’s “Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness” and “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever” and 2024’s “Deadpool & Wolverine,” but audiences were no longer showing up to theaters just because a new superhero adventure was gracing the big screen.

	“Audiences are tired of seeing the same thing. There are too many connected storylines, and it’s turning entertainment into homework,” says analyst Jeff Bock of Exhibitor Relations. “We need a fresh start.” 

	That’s part of the appeal of “Brand New Day,” which confirms there’s truly no such thing as Spider-Man fatigue. This Spidey adventure was promoted as a reset in the web-slinging series. That’s after the prior installment, “No Way Home,” ended on a massive cliffhanger: Tom Holland‘s Peter Parker made the difficult decision to erase his identity from the world in order to save the multiverse, leaving his girlfriend (Zendaya) and best friend Ned (Jacob Batalon) to forget about him. Demand — to find out the ramifications of Spider-Man’s fateful choice, and to be among the first to find out who Sadie Sink was playing in the film — was so intense that some locations of major theater chains were scheduling showtimes every 15 minutes from dusk to dawn. 

	What’s more impressive about the debut is “Brand New Day” didn’t play in Imax, the most ubiquitous of the premium large formats, because “The Odyssey” has the network’s entire domestic footprint for three weekends. “Spider-Man 4” dominated the other PLFs, though, establishing new opening weekend records for Dolby ($10 million domestically), 4DX ($17 million globally) and ScreenX ($14.4 million globally).
	

	“This weekend’s historic worldwide results remind me of what Clarence wrote to George Bailey in ‘It’s a Wonderful Life’: ‘Remember, no man is a failure who has friends,'” Sony’s motion picture group chair Tom Rothman said in a statement. “‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ is fundamentally a movie about friendship, about the balm of connection in all our lives, and that is resonant to audiences of all ages and all around the world. In troubled times, Sony is very proud to have united the world in celebrating a film about hope.”

	Holland’s run as Spider-Man is the rare series to keep improving upon the last at the box office. His first outing, 2017’s “Homecoming,” launched to $117 million domestically and ended its run with $880 million worldwide. Then 2019’s sequel “Far From Home” ignited to $92 million domestically but powered to $1.13 billion worldwide. And of course, “No Way Home” was colossal with $1.9 billion worldwide. That film was especially huge because all three Spider-Men — Holland, Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield — shared the screen in a crossover event for the ages. Holland’s future with the character is uncertain (he said recently that a succession plan is already in the works), but it’s hard to imagine the studio will want to part with the 30-year-old actor after this historic weekend. Meanwhile, Marvel will build on the success of “Brand New Day” with “Avengers: Doomsday,” which reunites a smattering of superheroes (and reintroduces Robert Downey Jr. not as Iron Man but as the villain Doctor Doom) in December.

	Elsewhere, “The Odyssey” has surpassed $911 million at the box office, including $395.5 million domestically and $515 million overseas. “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” will imminently be the fourth and fifth releases of the year to surpass $1 billion, following June’s “Toy Story 5” ($1.02 billion) and April’s “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” ($1.001 billion) and “Michael” ($1.001 billion).

	The staying power of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey” will determine whether this summer will become the second since COVID to cross the coveted $4 billion milestone. And with blockbusters like “Dune 3” and “Avengers: Doomsday” on the way, Hollywood is hoping that yearly grosses will hit $10 billion for the first time in the post-pandemic era. Revenues used to regularly eclipse the $10 billion mark before the great movie theater reset.
	

	“This milestone weekend sets up a tremendous month of August,” says Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends, Paul Dergarabedian. “The likelihood of a $4 billion summer and a $10 billion year just went up exponentially.”

schema.headline: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Swings to Mind-Blowing $355 Million Debut, Second-Biggest Opening Weekend in Box Office History

title: ‘Wonder Man’ Co-Creator Says ‘Contracts Were Signed, Schedules Were Cleared’ Before Marvel Series Was Canceled: ‘This Is Not a Marketing Stunt’
description: “Wonder Man” showrunner and co-creator Andrew Guest took to TikTok on Saturday to thank fans and share his thoughts about the Marvel Television dram
body:
“Wonder Man” showrunner and co-creator Andrew Guest took to TikTok on Saturday to thank fans and share his thoughts about the Marvel Television drama’s cancellation.

	“Just want to say I’ve been listening,” Guest said. “I appreciate you all. I feel how you all feel, and I just want to clear up when I can here. This is not a marketing stunt. There is no movie in the works, and [Destin Daniel Cretton’s] schedule and no one’s schedule was an issue. Yahya [Abdul Mateen II], Destin, Sir Ben [Kingsley] and I all loved making this show. All felt passionately about continuing to do it, and were eager to. Contracts were signed, schedules were cleared.”
	

	He added, “The writers’ room was supposed to start this month. The production was supposed to begin early next year, and there was a decision made internally between Disney and Marvel that this didn’t make sense for them, even though a few months ago it did. And that’s essentially all I really know.”


	Variety exclusively reported in late July that “Wonder Man” was canceled at Disney+ before the launch of its second season. The move was a sudden change of course for Disney, which announced in March that the show would return to Disney+ for Season 2.

	Star Yahya Abdul Mateen II, who earned an Emmy for his role as superpowered aspiring actor Simon Williams, shared a reaction of his own when news dropped that “Wonder Man” was canceled. He wrote on Instagram, “Word just dropped that Wonder Man won’t be coming back for Season 2. (And if you don’t knowww, now ya knoww!) That’s life, right? Everything will shake out.”
	

	Along with Abdul-Mateen II and Ben Kingsley, other Season 1 cast members included X Mayo, Demetrius Grosse, Zlatko Burić, Arian Moayed and Olivia Thirlby. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” director Destin Daniel Cretton co-created “Wonder Man” with Guest and helmed the first episode.

	The show’s logline reads, “Aspiring Hollywood actor Simon Williams (Abdul-Mateen II) is struggling to get his career off the ground. During a chance meeting with Trevor Slattery (Kingsley), an actor whose biggest roles may be well behind him, Simon learns legendary director Von Kovak (Burić) is remaking the superhero film ‘Wonder Man.’ These two actors at opposite ends of their careers doggedly pursue life-changing roles in this film as audiences get a peek behind the curtain of the entertainment industry.”

title: Stassi Schroeder Takes Us Inside That Explosive ‘House of Stassi’ Finale: ‘I Felt Like Julius Caesar’
description: Stassi Schroeder has come a long way from her days backhanding her castmates, dating chuds and lording over SUR like an icy sorority queen on “Vande
body:
Stassi Schroeder has come a long way from her days backhanding her castmates, dating chuds and lording over SUR like an icy sorority queen on “Vanderpump Rules.” She’s now a mother of two, married to the charming (and astonishingly tolerant) Beau Clark, pens New York Times bestsellers and hosts a hit podcast. She’s also the star and executive producer of her own reality show, “House of Stassi,” currently streaming on Hulu and Disney+.
	

	“This is not ‘Vanderpump Rules’ and this is not ‘The Kardashians,’ this is somewhere in the middle,” Schroeder tells Variety.


	Throughout the debut season of “House of Stassi,” we see Schroeder struggle mightily with trying to balance motherhood, family and her professional life, leading to clashes with her hubby Clark, who feels underappreciated and emasculated after stepping away from his casting job to be a stay-at-home dad raising their kids; her sister, Georgi, who’s still reeling from a divorce, crashing at Schroeder and Clark’s home and almost certainly hooking up with Clark’s best mate Rob; and Katie Maloney and Kristina Kelly, her former “Vanderpump Rules” ride-or-dies, who lightly disapprove of her dismissiveness toward Beau. There’s also her longtime pal Taylor Strecker (and her pregnant wife Taylor Donohue), Beau’s Italian half-sister Georgia (who’s also crashing with Schroeder and Clark) and, yes, Rob, a dude pushing 50 who only dates twenty-somethings.  



	Things come to a head in the eighth and final episode of the season, titled “Queen Mary’s Revenge.” The entire gang (sans Donohue, who’s beaming in via iPad) is having dinner aboard the historic Queen Mary ship in Long Beach, California, when they all hatch a plan, conceived by Maloney, to confront Schroeder over her treatment of Clark, who’s spent the entire season lamenting the dearth of affection in their relationship and missing his 9 to 5. Nearly everyone at the table, Clark included, airs their grievances toward Schroeder and, needless to say, it does not go well.
	

	“I felt like Julius Caesar. Literally,” Schroeder says of the intervention. “Katie Maloney was Brutus, and Beau fell for the bait. I watched it happen and was like, ‘How are you falling for this?’ Kristina Kelly was like, ‘Poor Beau!’ and Beau was like, ‘Poor me!’ and I was like, ‘Oh my god, my life is flashing before my eyes right now.’ I did not spend over three-and-a-half years working on this for it to lead here. It was wild. I felt very hopeless and devastated in that moment.”

	Schroeder says she felt like all the progress Clark and her had made during the latter part of the season — including a romantic date they went on at the cemetery where he’d proposed — all “unraveled so quickly,” and that she and Maloney, the architect of the intervention, still have some work to do to fully mend things.

	“I’ve said some things to her and we’re good, but I still have some more to say to her,” Schroeder explains. “I also think she wasn’t doing it to be cruel or to make me look bad. I think she was looking at Tom Schwartz and her marriage in terms of how resentment can build over something. I think Katie saw herself in Beau and Kristina saw herself in Beau, in the sense that they hadn’t gotten what they needed at certain times, so that was their concern. I choose to look at it like that versus friends who are out to get you.”



	

					Beau Clark and Stassi Schroeder in the “House of Stassi” finale.
									Freeform
	



	After the gang gives her the business, Schroeder’s “Dark Passenger” comes out — her name for her explosive alter ego — and she finds herself lashing out at everyone before crumbling into a ball of tears on the floor of the ship. But don’t be alarmed: She is adamant that she and Clark are in a good place and, even though she infamously dropped the D word on “Vanderpump Villa,” that is not in the cards for the couple.

	“As far as what it took afterwards, I feel comfortable being on a reality show with [Clark] because no matter what, we have that foundation where we do have each other,” Schroeder maintains, adding, “My parents have both been married four times each and his mom has been married a few times, and that was something we discussed. Unless someone does — you know what I mean — you can work through almost anything when you have respect and love for each other, so it makes having those fights and arguments on-camera easy to deal with because I know that we’re going to be fine. That might not make sense to someone who’s not on reality TV, but it does for me.”
	

	And as far as the future of “House of Stassi” and where the friend group goes from there, Schroeder shares that she wants the cast to remain intact and may have some tricks up her sleeve as far as getting the show renewed for a second season.

	“I hope that this [cast] remains intact, but it’s going to follow the stories that are naturally happening. So, if someone isn’t talking to the rest of us then that story is going to fall off,” says Schroeder. “It’s time I let everybody else’s stories also spider out, and I would like to go to each of them and pick up where we left off.”

	What about her and Clark? “It took time after filming to have those difficult conversations again and force ourselves to refocus and see what the real issues were,” she admits. “And we still have those conversations.”

title: Emmy-Nominated Stars Hannah Einbinder and Paul W. Downs on the Legacy of ‘Hacks’ and Which Character Needs a Spinoff First
description: Hannah Einbinder says working with Gillian Anderson on the new film “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma” has actually given her a new perspective
body:
Hannah Einbinder says working with Gillian Anderson on the new film “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma” has actually given her a new perspective on the end of “Hacks” and its legacy.

	“Doing all this press with Gillian for the movie, she talks about ‘X-Files’ constantly,” Einbinder tells Variety‘s Awards Circuit Podcast. “She’s asked about it constantly. It’s made me feel like, ‘oh, I’m gonna talk about “Hacks” for the rest of my life!’ I’m so happy that will always be something that I can come back to and meditate on and express gratitude for. When you are a part of something that has a deeply connected base of people who love it, that stays.”
	

	Meanwhile, given how many photo shoots and events Paul W. Downs and his “Hacks” co-star Megan Stalter seem to show up at, why isn’t there a Jimmy and Kayla spinoff in the works?


	“I would love for it to happen, and I have said this: You know we had a very specific plan for the way we wanted to end the story in the finale,” he says. “It’s such it’s so much pressure to deliver a satisfying ending … so, even to the last minute, even though we had this plan for a long time, we were like, ‘Should we stretch it out? Should we do two half seasons?’ But in the end, I’m so happy we stuck to our guns, and it resonated with people the way that it did. And because of that, I don’t I don’t want anything else to come after. I want that to be the last thing people remember.”

	When grilled about “Jimmy and Kayla,” he adds, “getting to play these characters and having these characters evolve as much as they have over the five seasons has been so gratifying that it’s terrifying to think there won’t be more between the two of us. But I think it would have to be something different.”
	

	OK … we’re getting somewhere. So what might a “Hacks” spinoff look like? “There’s so many characters in the show that if we could do a universe, I want to see Mayor Jo in her first election. I want to see Marty coming to to Vegas in the ’70s.”

	Einbinder likes the Mayor Jo idea. “‘Better Call Saul’ vibes,” she says. “Her just being a fucking absolute criminal. Are you kidding?  I’m in the freaking seats with the popcorn on that one.”

	Give it time. Maybe we’ll wear them down! But for now, we’ve got Downs and Einbinder on this week’s Awards Circuit Podcast, where they talk more about the “Hacks” ending and what they’ve got in store next. Plus, they take the 10 Questions quiz!

	But first, on the Roundtable, Variety TV critic Aramide Tinubu joins us to give some of her summer TV picks and hot takes on the Emmy noms. Listen below!

	He might be a bit biased, but Downs raves about Einbinder’s part in the upcoming slasher film “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma,” which opens August 7. “I’ll give you the review,” he says. “This is a pull quote now from Variety. Absolutely beautiful, absolutely terrifying and absolutely funny. And Hannah is a revelation. She is such a star. I’m not even kidding. The stuff that she does, her range being on display yet again in this is really impressive.”

	As for Downs, Lucia Aniello and Jen Statsky, the trio has a number of projects in the works — including one in development with Kaley Cuoco — although she’s busy on something else right now, so schedules will have to align for their project. And then the trio also has another project they’re working on for HBO.

	“I can say it’s a it’s a limited series,” he says. “It’s an hourlong limited. I can say that. So it’s a slight tone shift, but there’s definitely going to be humor.”

	Einbinder says she’d be game to join them again for this next project. “I told Paul, Jen and Lucia that I want to be their non-problematic Rob Schneider. I just want to pop up in everything they do forever.”

	Meanwhile, Einbinder says she’s still thinking a lot about her time on “Hacks,” and how she found a video that she recorded for herself in Season 1. Now it feels like a bit of a time capsule: “It was in my trailer, and the sound is pretty muffled, and it’s kind of a shitty video, but I just was kind of reflecting, like kind of a diary, and one of the things that I said was ‘I think these people are going to mean so much to me.’”
	

	Einbinder’s come a long way in those six years since “Hacks” first became a reality. “Most nights when I get into bed and feel the relief of making it back to my bed at the end of a long day, I go, ‘wow.’ I just am filled with gratitude. This experience has made so much possible for me in every conceivable way. On an emotional level, obviously we have a very strong bond. When I was auditioning for Ava initially, I was opening for other comics on the road. That went away because of COVID, and the job I had before that was working at a coffee shop, and that also went away. I was just really, ‘I actually don’t know what I’m gonna do.’ And so just on every level, [this success] has never been lost on me.”


	10 QUESTIONS WITH HANNAH EINBINDER and PAUL W. DOWNS:

	1. Childhood nickname: Einbinder: “‘Pud,’ short for ‘Pudding.’ My parents called me that.” Downs: “‘Chubb.’ I think it came from my love of pasta and pizza. I think it honestly came from my love of Swiss Miss. I would take Swiss Miss packets with half and half, and I would make like a sludge that I would drink. It was my version of child cocaine, I guess.”

	2. Something you loved as a kid but can’t believe you were into it now: Downs: “I used to kind of collect these, they were basically little figurines that were like a dragon or an Excalibur or a wizard, and they were on amethyst. They were sold at a kiosk at the Rockaway Town Square Mall, and I was into these bizarre — I don’t know what that is. Fantasy figurines. They were also very like Sedona. You know, they were very like hippie figurines. I can’t believe I was so into that” Einbinder: “I have done so much inner child work that I have love and affection for the things that I maybe was into. I took baton. I had a baton unit. I was very into baton at one time. I did baton classes. I learned from a stripper named Heather. Thank you, Heather. She taught baton on the side. She was like, ‘I do flaming baton at my where I dance,’ and we were like, ‘We want to come see you dance, Heather!’ And she was like, ‘It’s not for kids.’”

	3. Go-to Karaoke or sing-in-the-shower song: Einbinder: “‘What’s Up,’ by 4 Non Blondes.” Downs: “‘All I Wanna Do’ by Sheryl Crow. It’s a real crowd pleaser.”

	4. Give me an alternate title for your show: [Not asked]

	5. What’s your secret talent?: Downs: “I can give a good massage.” Einbinder: “I can create a bubble ring underwater. Or a smoke ring. I can do that too. But that’s featured in the show ‘Hacks.’”
	

	6. Favorite ice cream flavor: Downs: “As a kid, I loved strawberry. Now I want like a like a dark chocolate double fudge chunk.” Einbinder: “Mint chip.”

	7. The one item you couldn’t live without: Einbinder: “Cell phone.” Downs: “I was gonna say toothpaste. You really want toothpaste.”

	8. What TV show in all of history do you wish you were a cast member of?: Einbinder: “‘Sopranos,’ ‘Mad Men.’” Downs: “Some of my favorite shows like ‘Arrested Development’ or ‘Succession’ or ‘Fleabag,’ I don’t know that I want to be on those shows. I think I want to be on ‘Friends.’ I think I would have had a blast.”

	9. Fictional character you most admire: [Not asked]

	10. Your favorite piece of advice: Einbinder: “‘Faster and funnier.’” Downs: “I’ve uttered those words. You know what else I uttered recently, and I’m taking a great piece of advice that Maya Angelou gave to Oprah, which is when someone tells you who they are, believe them the first time. I think that’s a really good piece of advice.”Variety’s “Awards Circuit” podcast, hosted by Clayton Davis, Jazz Tangcay, Emily Longeretta and Michael Schneider, who also produces, is your one-stop source for lively conversations about the best in film and television. Each episode, “Awards Circuit” features interviews with top film and TV talent and creatives, discussions and debates about awards races and industry headlines, and much more. Subscribe via Apple Podcasts, Stitcher, Spotify or anywhere you download podcasts.

title: Ariana Grande to Take ‘Step Back From Visibility’ After Tour Ends Amid ‘Public Scrutiny,’ Drops Out of ‘Sunday in the Park With George’ Musical
description: Ariana Grande is stepping out of the spotlight for an extended break after she wraps her Eternal Sunshine Tour, a rep for the actress and pop star t
body:
Ariana Grande is stepping out of the spotlight for an extended break after she wraps her Eternal Sunshine Tour, a rep for the actress and pop star told People. The rep’s statement cited “ongoing public scrutiny” as one of the reasons for the pause. 

	“Ariana will be taking a step back from visibility after she completes the Eternal Sunshine Tour,” Grande’s rep said. “She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny. This tour has been a beautiful experience for her. She loves her fans and has loved every minute of this tour so much.”
	

	People also reported that Grande has dropped out of Stephen Sondheim’s West End revival of “Sunday in the Park With George.” Grande was set to star alongside Jonathan Bailey in the production.


	The Eternal Sunshine Tour wraps on Sept. 1, meaning Grande is gunning for a break starting in the early fall. However, Grande is soon starring in “Focker-in-Law” alongside Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller. That film is positioned to be a holiday hit for Universal and arrives in theaters the day before Thanksgiving. It will most likely require a splashy promotional tour and many public appearances from Grande and her co-stars.

	Universal did not immediately comment on whether Grande’s plan will interfere with the “Focker-in-Law” press tour.  

	The “public scrutiny” mentioned by the rep could point to several things. In recent years, as Grande has risen to super stardom, her physical appearance has been put under the microscope in certain online circles. Her “Petal” music video, which was released on Friday, reignited fan concerns about her weight loss.
	

	Grande, a three-time Grammy winner and former child star of Nickelodeon favorites like “Victorious” and “Sam & Cat,” reached Hollywood A-list status with the 2024 release of the “Wicked” movie. Grande played Glinda, the good, opposite Cynthia Erivo’s Elphaba. The film was a cultural phenomenon, earning Academy Award nominations for best picture and best supporting actress for Grande. It also won two Oscars for best costume design and best production design. Grande and Erivo went on a globe-trotting press tour for the ages to promote the movie musical. The sequel “Wicked: For Good” was likewise a hit, but didn’t require as much promotional legwork from its stars.

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ and ‘The Odyssey’ Power Biggest Collective Weekend in Box Office History With $430 Million
description: A powerful one-two punch from “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey” has fueled the biggest collective weekend in box office history, with ro
body:
A powerful one-two punch from “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey” has fueled the biggest collective weekend in box office history, with roughly $430 million across all movies in the marketplace.

	Prior to this, the top three weekends were led by “Avengers: Endgame” ($402 million collectively), 2018’s “Avengers: Infinity War” ($314 million collectively) and 2015’s “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” ($313 million collectively). It’s a particularly exciting benchmark for the recently married Tom Holland and Zendaya, who star in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey.”
	

	“We have conquered a box-office milestone that seemed forever out of reach,” says Paul Dergarabedian, Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends. “This is now only the second $400 million-plus weekend in box office history.”


	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” the fourth comic-book adventure starring Holland as the web-slinging hero, exploded with $355 million in its domestic debut, ranking as the second-biggest opening of all time as well as the second movie in history to cross $300 million in a single weekend. “Brand New Day” nearly matched the opening weekend record held by 2019’s behemoth “Avengers: Endgame,” which ignited to an astounding $357 million. (And some analysts believe “Brand New Day” could end up eclipsing “Endgame’s” record when final numbers are tallied on Monday.) “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” already scored the largest preview haul with $72 million, as well as the biggest opening day with $168 million.

	However, “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” couldn’t have powered the overall weekend record alone. “The Odyssey” remained a force in its third frame with $51 million, a remarkable haul given the all-out frenzy around Peter Parker. Holdovers like Disney’s “Toy Story 5” and “Moana” and Universal’s “Minion & Monsters” also contributed to the fun. 
	

	“The combination of ‘Spider-Man’ and ‘The Odyssey’ — a legacy superhero sequel and a big original production — is taking the box office to new highs by a comfortable margin,” says David A. Gross, who publishes the box office newsletter FranchiseRe. “These are stunning numbers.” 

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” is the follow-up to 2021’s behemoth “Spider-Man: No Way Home,” which opened to $260 million (the third-biggest debut ever) and powered to $1.9 billion by the end of its run. And that was without China, a major market for Marvel movies. That film was huge because all three Spider-Men — Holland, Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield — shared the screen in a crossover event for the ages. Since “No Way Home” ended on a massive cliffhanger (Holland’s Peter Parker made the difficult decision to erase his identity from the world in order to save the multiverse), a ton of people have been waiting half a decade to find out what happens next. Critics and audiences were high on “Brand New Day,” which boasts a 90% on Rotten Tomatoes and “A” grade on CinemaScore exit polls — setting up the comic-book tentpole to dominate in theaters throughout the rest of August.

	“The Odyssey” continues to shatter expectations, too. Christopher Nolan‘s Greek epic has generated a remarkable $911 million worldwide after less than a month in theaters. It’s less than a week away from crossing the billion-dollar mark, underscoring Nolan’s ability to transform his movies into cultural events. “The Odyssey” will also surpass “The Dark Knight” ($1.008 billion) and 2012’s “The Dark Knight Rises” ($1.08 billion) as the director’s highest-grossing film of all time. Not bad for an adaptation of a nearly 3,000-year-old poem.

title: 21 Best Movies New to Streaming in August: ‘Michael,’ ‘Mother Mary,’ ‘Oppenheimer’ Back on Peacock and More
description:
Aug 2, 2026 8:59am PT	
	

	
		21 Best Movies New to Streaming in August: ‘Michael,’ ‘Mother Mary,’ ‘Oppenheimer’ Back on Peacock and
body:
Aug 2, 2026 8:59am PT	
	

	
		21 Best Movies New to Streaming in August: ‘Michael,’ ‘Mother Mary,’ ‘Oppenheimer’ Back on Peacock and More
	
	
			


			
			
	

									Everett Collection
	

		
	
				

	Looking to watch the biggest movies of the year? You’ll have to go to the theater this August to catch “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” but coming home is the Michael Jackson biopic “Michael” after a historic box office run earlier this year. The movie became the second title of 2026 to cross the $1 billion mark at the worldwide box office, and in doing so surpassed Christopher Nolan’s “Oppenheimer” as the highest-grossing movie biopic in history.

	Speaking of “Oppenheimer,” Nolan’s beloved Oscar winner returns to streaming this month courtesy of Peacock. The time is ripe, as the incredible success of “The Odyssey” has sparked demand from fans to stream other Nolan films from home.

	As for other 2026 titles joining “Michael” on streaming platforms this month, there’s A24’s “Mother Mary” with Anne Hathaway hitting HBO Max, the criminally under-seen “Is God Is” arriving on Prime Video, the charming romantic comedy “You, Me & Tuscany” debuting on Peacock and Billie Eilish’s “Hit Me Hard and Soft” concert movie launching on Paramount+.

	Read below for a full rundown of the biggest movies new to streaming this August.


			
			
	Michael (Aug. 10 on Starz)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Lions Gate/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	The King of Pop is headed to streaming. “Michael,” the musical biopic that follows Michael Jackson’s career, will begin streaming on Starz on Aug. 10 after grossing $1 billion at the worldwide box office this spring to become the highest-grossing biopic of all time. Directed by Antoine Fuqua and written by John Logan, “Michael” chronicles Jackson’s rise to fame, covering his involvement in the Jackson 5 band with his brothers in the 1960s to his “Bad” tour in the late 1980s. Jackson is played by his nephew, Jaafar Jackson, and as a child by Juliano Valdi, both making their film debuts.
		
			
			
	Oppenheimer (Aug. 13 on Peacock)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Universal/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	With Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” shattering box office expectations and heading to a $1 billion worldwide haul in movie theaters, now is the perfect time for his Oscar winner “Oppenheimer” to return to streaming on Peacock. The biographical drama earned $955 million at the worldwide box office in 2023 (a staggering haul for a three hour, R-rated biopic) and won seven Oscars, including best picture, director, actor for Cillian Murphy and supporting actor for Robert Downey Jr. The drama was named the best film of 2023 by Variety critic Owen Gleiberman.
		
			
			
	Mother Mary (Aug. 21 on HBO Max)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	David Lowery’s “Mother Mary,” starring Anne Hathaway as a damaged pop star seeking to reclaim her glory, did not set the box office on fire for A24 earlier this year. The movie’s $2.9 million gross disappointed, although here’s hoping more moviegoers discover its wicked charms on streaming this month when it debuts on HBO Max. The movie follows Hathaway as a pop star who, after abandoning her tour due to an existential crisis, seeks out an old friend and fashion designer, Sam (a hypnotizing Michaela Coel), who helped craft her public persona. “Mother Mary” features original songs written by Jack Antonoff, Charli xcx and FKA Twigs, who also appears in the film.
		
			
			
	Billie Eilish — Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour (Aug. 6 on Paramount+)
			
										
					Image Credit: Paramount				
					
				
	“Billie Eilish — Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour (Live)” will premiere Aug. 6 on Paramount+. The concert movie was released in theaters on May 8 and grossed $10 million in the United States and Canada, plus $27 million worldwide. Eilish co-directed alongside James Cameron. Filmed during Eilish’s shows on her sold-out headline tour, the project marks her third concert film. The performances were captured at two arenas: one in Manchester, England, and one in Phoenix, Arizona.
		
			
			
	You, Me & Tuscany (Aug. 7 on Peacock)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Universal/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Kat Coiro’s romantic comedy “You, Me & Tuscany” arrives on Peacock this month after earning $22 million in theaters worldwide earlier this year. Halle Bailey stars as an aspiring chef who finds herself squatting in a Tuscan villa by posing as the owner’s fiancé. Then she falls in love with the owner’s relative, played by “Bridgerton” favorite Regé-Jean Page. Variety’s review was mixed, with praise for the performers but notes for the script: “‘You, Me & Tuscany’ passes the time painlessly enough, but it’s never quite the escape it wants to be: It’s packaged so familiarly and so cautiously, we hardly believe its celebration of free, restlessly wandering impulse.”
		
			
			
	Camp Rock 3 (Aug. 13 on Disney+)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Disney+/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Disney revives one of its most classic franchises this month with the arrival of “Camp Rock 3,” which brings the Jonas Brothers back as the fictional band Connect 3 for a new story in which the group heads to the eponymous camp to find the opening act for their reunion tour. An official synopsis teases: “As campers vie for the chance to open for their favorite band, tensions rise and friendships are tested — leading to unexpected alliances, revelations and romances.”
		
			
			
	Is God Is (Aug. 19 on Prime Video)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©MGM/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Aleshea Harris’ directorial debut “Is God Is” was named one of the best movies of 2026 so far by Variety: “A marvelous writer, Harris is conversant in the languages of both ruthless exploitation cinema and radical feminist theatre, with filmmaking brio to match. Whatever she makes next, here’s hoping more attention is paid.” This “furiously visceral and caustically funny female revenge drama” centers on twin sisters (Tony winner Kara Young and Mallori Johnson) who seek revenge on the abusive father who wronged them. Sterling K. Brown, Janelle Monae and Vivica A. Fox co-star.
		
			
			
	The Last House (Aug. 7 on Netflix)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Wagner Moura and Greta Lee headline Netflix’s supernatural thriller “The Last House,” from director Louis Leterrier. The synopsis reads: “A family of four are suddenly sealed inside their home with no way out, and must work together to survive against both their dwindling resources and the mysterious, looming threat that is keeping them trapped.” Given the “trapped inside” vs. “outside threat” plot set up, don’t be surprised if “The Last House” becomes a Netflix blockbuster in the same vein as 2023’s “Leave the World Behind.”
		
			
			
	The Whisper Man (Aug. 28 on Netflix)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Netflix’s crime thriller “The Whisper Man” is produced by “Avengers” duo Joe and Anthony Russo and based on the New York Times bestselling novel by Alex North. The synopsis reads: “When his 8-year-old son is abducted, a widowed crime writer looks to his estranged father, a retired former police detective, for help, only to discover a connection with the decades-old case of a convicted serial killer known as The Whisper Man.” The cast features Robert De Niro, Michelle Monaghan, Adam Scott, Hamish Linklater, Owen Teague, Acston Luca Porto and Will Brill.
		
			
			
	Don’t Say Good Luck (Aug. 14 on Netflix)
			
										
					Image Credit: Netflix				
					
				
	The latest collaboration between Netflix and Adam Sandler’s production company Happy Madison may surprise fans. Starring Sandler’s daughter Sunny opposite Melanie Lynskey and Max Greenfield, “Don’t Say Good Luck” is a coming-of-age comedy drama about a high school theater student whose pursuit to land the lead role in a musical is complicated by her mother’s illness. The movie comes from Julia Hart, the director behind “Miss Stevens,” “Fast Color,” “Stargirl” and “I’m Your Woman,” all of which are miles away from the juvenile humor that Sandler’s production company is known for churning out. 
		
			
			
	The Christophers (Aug. 22 on Hulu)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Steven Soderbergh’s “The Christophers” stars Ian McKellen and Michaela Coel and centers on the children of a famous artist who hire a forger to complete some of his unfinished works so that they can increase their inheritance upon his death. The movie was named a Variety Critic’s Pick: “In what could have easily been a play, but is far more satisfying on screen, the two English actors attempt to outwit one another as an aging artist and the forger hired to complete a key project from his past.”
		
			
			
	The Wizard of the Kremlin (Aug. 14 on Hulu)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Paul Dano, Alicia Vikander and Jude Law team up in Olivier Assayas’ political thriller “The Wizard of the Kremlin,” based on Giuliano da Empoli’s bestseller of the same name. Law takes on the role of Vladimir Putin while Dano plays Vadim Baranov, a young artist-turned-TV producer who unexpectedly becomes Putin’s spin doctor in the early 1990s after the USSR’s collapse.
		
			
			
	Desert Warrior (Aug. 28 on Hulu)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	The Rupert Wyatt-directed epic “Desert Warrior” was an infamous box office flop this spring, but perhaps all the headlines over the movie’s theatrical demise will increase interest on streaming when it arrives on Hulu this month. The movie is the most expensive feature film to come out of the Middle East to date. “Desert Warrior” is set 1,500 years ago and picks up in the aftermath of emperor Kisra II (Ben Kingsley) ordering his subjects to surrender their daughters to serve as concubines. Princess Hind (Aiysha Hart) links up with a nameless bandit (Anthony Mackie) to avoid persecution as the duo is chased across the desert by the emperor’s bloodthirsty commander (Sharlto Copley).
		
			
			
	The Ribbon Hero (Aug. 8 on Netflix)
			
										
					Image Credit: Netflix				
					
				
	The description for the Netflix original anime feature “The Ribbon Hero” reads: “Yuki Igarashi, regarded as one of the industry’s most versatile animators, directs the film. He first drew wide attention for the sophisticated animation he handled alone as key animator on the ending sequence of ‘Jujutsu Kaisen’ Season 1. His directorial debut, Star Wars: Visions – Lop & Ochō,’ received high praise in Japan and abroad for its delicate storytelling and dynamic action scenes. ‘The Ribbon Hero’ marks Igarashi’s first time directing a feature-length film. Bringing together a team of highly skilled creators, the film depicts the story of a lone hero who chooses to defy a harsh destiny, set in a delicately crafted world and brought to life through polished action.”
		
			
			
	The Strangers: Chapter 2 (Aug. 7 on HBO Max)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Lions Gate/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Renny Harlin’s “The Strangers” trilogy continues with a second installment that finds Maya (Madeline Petsch) wounded in a hospital, mourning the death of her fiancé at the end of 2024’s “Chapter 1.” But she can’t sit around healing for too long, as the three masked killers are almost immediately after her again. Instead of running, Maya eventually chooses to stand her ground and fight back.
		
			
			
	Normal (Aug. 14 on HBO Max)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Magnolia Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Ben Wheatley teams up with Bob Odenkirk and “John Wick” screenwriter Derek Kolstad to helm “Normal,” an action comedy in which Odenkirk’s new sheriff finds himself in over his head when he starts investigating a botched bank robbery. Henry Winkler and Lena Headey also star in the movie. From Variety’s review: “‘Normal’ is pretty much exactly what you’d expect, just a lot more fun… the movie lets audiences think it’s going to be one thing for the first half-hour or so, then turns on a dime once the bank is robbed.”
		
			
			
	The Last Sunrise (Aug. 26 on Prime Video)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©MGM/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	From Amazon Prime Video: “Based on the beloved novel, ‘The Last Sunrise’ follows Ry (Maia Reficco), a college student with a chronic illness, on a summer escape to Mallorca with her mother (Eva Longoria). As she unexpectedly falls for Julián (Fernando Lindez) and begins to embrace living in the moment, her worsening condition and long-hidden family secrets threaten to unravel everything before the summer ends.”
		
			
			
	Midwinter Break (Aug. 10 on Netflix)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Focus Features/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Lesley Manville and Ciarán Hinds play a married couple come undone during a trip to Amsterdam in drama thriller “Midwinter Break,” adapted from the 2017 novel of the same name by Bernard MacLaverty. From Variety’s review: “The director, Polly Findlay, presents her film in a fluid and fastidious prestige-teleplay-of-the-week way. She creates a generous space for her actors, who turn what might have been a rather staid movie — and still, at times, is — into a meticulous duet.”
		
			
			
	Five Nights at Freddy’s 2 (Aug. 3 on Netflix)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Universal/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	The Blumhouse horror sequel “Five Nights at Freddy’s 2” arrives on Netflix this month after debuting on Peacock earlier this year. Josh Hutcherson, Matthew Lillard and Elizabeth Lail star in the horror feature from returning franchise director Emma Tammi. The movie earned $239 million at the worldwide box office last winter, good enough to put a third movie into development. 
		
			
			
	Good Fortune (Aug. 21 on Prime Video)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Lions Gate/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Written, directed by and starring Aziz Ansari, “Good Fortune” follows Gabriel (Keanu Reeves), a well-meaning but inept angel who meddles in the lives of a struggling worker (Ansari) and a wealthy venture capitalist (Seth Rogen). Sandra Oh and Keke Palmer also star. The film marks Ansari’s feature directorial debut following his stint as the star and creator of Netflix’s “Master of None.” From Variety’s review: “The comedian borrows tropes from vintage studio movies — including meddling angels and ‘Freaky Friday’-style identity swaps — to make a timely critique of the gig economy.”
		
			
			
	Asphalt City (Aug. 3 on Netflix)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Roadside Attractions/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	“Asphalt City” stars Tye Sheridan as Ollie Cross, a young paramedic in New York City who is mentored by Sean Penn’s more-experienced EMT. The two are forced to face extreme violence during their shifts, from blood-soaked gunshot wounds to disturbing scenes of domestic violence and life-threatening pregnancies, forcing Ollie to confront his beliefs about life and death. Legendary boxer Mike Tyson also stars in the film as Chief Burroughs, Sheridan and Penn’s superior officer.

title: Idaho In-N-Out Mass Shooter Identified, Confirmed Deceased
description:
Idaho In-N-Out Mass Shooting
                          Gunman Identified, Dead From Self-Inflicte
body:
Idaho In-N-Out Mass Shooting
                          Gunman Identified, Dead From Self-Inflicted Gunshot Wound
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 2, 2026
                            1:30 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Officials have identified the suspect in the mass shooting which occurred at an Idaho In-N-Out Burger as 24-year-old Chad Williams, leaving at least three people dead and seven injured.
      
    
            Authorities revealed his identity during a press conference Sunday and confirm he is deceased from a self-inflicting gunshot wound. According to officials, investigators are continuing to look into the incident timeline, process evidence, and conduct interviews.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Instagram Media.
      
    
            As we previously reported ... the mayhem began Saturday afternoon at the burger joint in Twin Falls -- a city in southern Idaho -- where the gunman opened fire, officials said.
      

            Twin Falls spokesperson, Josh Palmer, told TMZ ... police received a call of an active shooter and quickly responded, but the shooter had already exited the restaurant and fled the immediate area.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Instagram Media.
      
    
            A motorist filmed the shooter with a cell phone camera walking to a white car while carrying a long gun. The suspect opened the driver-side door and popped the trunk, then walked to the rear of the car and reached inside the trunk. Fearing the suspect might be reaching for another firearm, the motorist took off.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            In-N-Out President Lynsi Snyder remembered the fallen employee and slammed the shooter as a "disgusting human who doesn't value the lives of others or his own."
      
    
            Police were interviewing numerous witnesses and canvassing for video at retail shops near the crime scene. Investigators were also trying to identify the suspect and determine a motive. Palmer said there were no other shooters and the threat to the public was over.

title: Nolan Wells Case: Possible Sighting of Boat in Newly Surfaced Video
description:
Nolan Wells Case
                          Possible Sighting of Boat in Newly Surfaced Video
body:
Nolan Wells Case
                          Possible Sighting of Boat in Newly Surfaced Video
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 2, 2026
                            10:49 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 2, 2026
                                1:31 PM PDT
                                    
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            A newly surfaced video from Horn Island on July 4 may provide a potential clue in the search for Nolan Wells, with footage appearing to show the boat he was allegedly last seen on.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Instagram Media.
      
    
            At the end of this clip, the "Mac Daddy" boat is clearly seen -- and appears to match the footage obtained by TMZ from the same day ... which could be the final sighting of Nolan before his disappearance.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The clip was posted by a person who said they captured the footage on July 4th at 11:17 AM, before the area became crowded. In our video, Metadata shows the video was recorded at 2:23 PM ... making this sighting way earlier in the day.
      

        
                    
                  
      
    
            In the video we previously obtained, the man wearing trunks matching the color of the ones Nolan was wearing in the infamous July 4 pic was with his friends on a boat and you can also see a couple of older adults also onboard the boat ... however in this new video, the adults seemingly don't appear to be the same.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The possible match has sparked renewed attention online, though it has not been confirmed whether the boat in the new footage is the same vessel connected to Nolan’s disappearance.
      
    
            The video comes as investigators continue working to piece together Nolan’s final known movements and determine what happened in the hours surrounding his disappearance.
      
    
            The boat’s appearance and location have raised questions, but officials have not publicly confirmed any connection between the vessel in the video and the ongoing investigation.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            As you know, Nolan disappeared after those friends left, and his body was found July 6 on the Horn Island shoreline. No witnesses have, at least publicly, reported seeing him after 4:30 PM on July 4.
      
    
            The boy's parents laid him to rest July 20 at Center Pointe Church in Ocean Springs, Mississippi, in a service officiated by Rev. Al Sharpton ... where he and Tyler Perry each offered $50K for information leading to a conviction in Nolan's death.

title: Ariana Grande Plans to Step Back From Public Life After Tour Ends Amid Criticism
description:
Ariana Grande
                          Leaving Spotlight After Tour Amid Health Scrutiny
body:
Ariana Grande
                          Leaving Spotlight After Tour Amid Health Scrutiny
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 2, 2026
                            1:26 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Ariana Grande is reportedly stepping away from the spotlight ... as concern and commentary surrounding her appearance reaches a fever pitch.
      
    
            The singer plans to "take a step back from visibility" after wrapping her "Eternal Sunshine Tour" in London on September 1, her rep tells PEOPLE ... blaming the "endless, ongoing public scrutiny" surrounding her public appearances.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The news comes after Jameela Jamil sounded the alarm Saturday over Ariana's appearance in her newly released "Petal" music video ... claiming the pop star is "possibly dying right in front of us."
      

                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The 'Good Place' actress compared the situation to the trolley problem ... acknowledging that commenting on Ariana's body could hurt her mental health, while arguing that staying silent could normalize what she deems is an unhealthy image for millions of young and impressionable fans.
      
    
            Jameela criticized the video's styling for what she sees as deliberately emphasizing Ariana's frame with belts and corsets ... and claimed images of the singer are already circulating on pro-anorexia websites, where some teenage girls are calling her appearance "goals."
      
    
            She also questioned whether Ariana has the support needed to deal with a potentially deadly eating disorder ... though Ariana has never said she has anorexia -- and Jameela offered no evidence she does.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Ariana has not responded to Jameela's claims ... a source close to the singer told PEOPLE she performs her highly physical show "healthily and successfully at a very high level night after night."
      
    
            Her rep added that Ariana plans to finish the tour "healthily and happily" before taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            That break will cost fans one highly anticipated performance ... the outlet also reported Ariana has dropped out of next summer's West End revival of "Sunday in the Park with George," which would have reunited her with "Wicked" costar Jonathan Bailey.
      
    
            Ariana has repeatedly pushed back against commentary about her body over the years ... reminding fans in 2023 that the appearance people once considered her "healthiest" actually came during an unhealthy period in her life.
